A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TaxoNet work, and all pages are readable. However, v1 includes supplementary Sections 7–11, while v2 ends with references despite retaining appendix pointers. Main-text changes and omissions from the supplied PDFs are verifiable; any separately existing v2 supplement cannot be assessed.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, geographic-transfer, open-set, ablation and foundation-model comparison results, plus supplementary sensitivity and random-seed experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental results in Tables 1–5 and adds results for previously unreported ablation configurations on iNat-Plantae and NAFlora-Mini.

M1.justification: The central margin specification changes. V1 uses blended empirical/effective-number priors and a negative power-scaled margin in Equation 5 and Algorithm 1. V2 specifies positive learned margins from log-normalized empirical frequencies, with an explicit normalization and corresponding regularizer. The backbone and norm-guided sampling remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish retraining.

E1.justification: Both retain Auto-Arborist's three regions, iNat-Plantae and NAFlora-Mini, covering taxonomic classification, geographic transfer, hierarchical evaluation and unknown-taxon rejection. The added ablation entries reuse existing datasets and tasks. BIOSCAN-1M is newly cited, not evaluated.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in Tables 1–5 is unchanged. However, the supplied v2 omits v1 Table 10's AA-Central foundation-model comparisons, including the additional description-assisted GPT-4o and Gemini variants. These distinct prompting comparators are not reported elsewhere in v2.

E3.justification: V2 consistently specifies logit scale s=32, resolving v1's conflicting s=64 in Section 3.2 versus s=32 in its experimental setup and supplement. This is a reported-setting correction, not evidence of rerunning experiments. Main input dimensions, batch settings, metrics and open-set calibration remain unchanged; supplementary precision/F1 evaluations are no longer supplied.

E4.justification: Table 1 extends three existing component-ablation configurations to iNat-Plantae and NAFlora-Mini. Conversely, v2 omits the separate regularization-weight and base-margin sensitivity studies in v1 Tables 6–7, substantially reducing documented hyperparameter analysis. The embedding-norm analysis and success/failure cases remain.

E5.justification: V1 reports four random seeds, {0, 1, 42, 2025}, their individual results, the default seed and an interpretation of variability in supplementary Section 9 and Table 8. V2 supplies none of this, removing the entire disclosed repeated-run check. This does not establish that fewer runs were performed.

E6.justification: All previously populated numerical entries in main Tables 1–5 are unchanged. V2 fills nine ablation cells, including iNat-Plantae scores of 78.91, 80.01 and 81.08. However, supplementary sensitivity, seed and per-class outcomes from v1 Tables 6–8 and 10–11 are absent, substantially changing the reported evidence without establishing improved headline performance.

T1.justification: Both propositions and their proofs in Section 4 are essentially retained. Formal changes are localized to the margin definitions in Section 3.2, removal of the stated softplus exponent condition greater than one, and replacement of proportionality with equality in the prototype-gradient decomposition. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: V1 presents introducing the named Open-World Ecological Taxonomy Challenge as a primary contribution. V2 removes that framework-novelty claim and centers its abstract, contribution list and conclusion on dual-margin learning for fine-grained, long-tailed plant recognition. This substantially narrows the contribution framing while retaining the principal empirical superiority claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation that large logit scales can aggravate gradient imbalance. It omits supplementary qualifications about sensitivity to tiny test classes, harmful larger base margins and potentially noisy description-heavy prompts. The main head–tail tradeoff, visual failure explanations and BioCLIP training-overlap discussion remain.

D1.justification: The missing supplement removes Algorithm 1, dataset split/count statistics, the 30-epoch AdamW configuration, learning-rate schedule, weight decay, augmentation probabilities, regularization weight and full prompting instructions. Main-text backbone and batch details remain, but the supplied v2 is substantially less reproducible. These are disclosure losses, not established changes to execution.

R1.justification: V2 adds a Hierarchical Taxonomy discussion and the BIOSCAN-1M citation, and softens Auto-Arborist's positioning from the only relevant large-scale repository to one of a few. The medical-diagnosis and AdamW references associated with omitted supplementary material disappear. Most related-work coverage remains, and BioCLIP's bibliographic rewrite represents the same comparator.

P1.justification: V2 changes the title and author list and extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition and conclusion. It reorganizes the contribution list, adds a hierarchical-taxonomy subsection and consolidates the margin explanation. Much of the evaluation narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: The document is extensively reformatted from two columns to one, with resized and relocated displays and side captions. Figure 1 is redrawn around closed-set, hierarchical and open-set regimes. Figures 2–4 retain identical image content. The supplementary algorithm, Tables 6–11 and prompt-template Figure 5 are absent.

improvement.justification: For the supplied PDFs, clearer framing, a more coherent margin specification and additional ablation results do not outweigh the loss of essential supplementary evidence. V2 leaves training and prompting details, sensitivity checks, seed results and detailed comparisons unavailable while still referring readers to an appendix. This substantially weakens reproducibility and robustness assessment; unchanged headline scores do not demonstrate benefits from the revised loss specification.
